title: Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the \bar{M} point in 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene
authors: Giovanna Feraco, Przemysław Przybysz, Oreste De Luca, Ying Wang, Pavel Dudin, José Avila, Jianting Ye, Paweł Dąbrowski, Paweł J. Kowalczyk, Jagoda Sławińska, Petra Rudolf, Antonija Grubišić-Čabo
abstract: The emergence of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the so-called magic angle reveals a range of intriguing phases, such as superconductivity and Mott insulating states, resulting from electrons entering a correlated state. This establishes twisted bilayer graphene as an excellent platform for exploring correlation effects in many-body phases and across various twist angles. However, in most cases, the twist angle is not an easy parameter to control because it exhibits structural instabilities such as relaxation and reconstruction that reduce the correlation effects. Here, we report the unexpected appearance of a flat band at the \bar{M} point far from the Fermi level in a 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene, directly visualized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our work is the first observation of flat bands away from the \bar{K} point in twisted bilayer graphene and highlights the need to probe the entire Brillouin zone to fully capture electronic states in twisted structures.
summary: This work reports the first direct observation of a flat electronic band at the M point in 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene using nano-ARPES. The observed feature cannot be explained by standard theoretical models (TB or DFT), suggesting that structural relaxations or local inhomogeneities are crucial for understanding correlated phases in moiré materials.
main_problem: To investigate the electronic structure of twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) beyond the conventional focus near the K point, specifically observing and understanding a flat band at the M point.
main_result: The authors report the first observation of a flat band at the M point in 2.4° TBG using nano-ARPES, which could not be reproduced by standard tight-binding or DFT calculations.
method: The study combines angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) experiments with theoretical modeling using tight-binding (TB) and Density Functional Theory (DFT).
model_or_system: The system is twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) at a 2.4° twist angle. Theoretical models utilize atomistic $\pi$-orbital tight-binding methods and DFT, while experiments are conducted at the SOLEIL synchrotron.
key_observables: Electronic band structure, flat band dispersion (or lack thereof), Fermi velocity, and spectral weight along high-symmetry paths ($\Gamma-	ext{M}-K-\Gamma$).
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta = 2.4^\circ$), temperature ($T = 70$ K), and the comparison between experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.
main_assumptions: The initial theoretical models assume an ideal, rigid lattice structure, which is contradicted by the experimental observation of the M-point flat band.
figures_summary: Figures show nano-ARPES data confirming a weakly dispersive feature at the M point, while theoretical calculations (TB and DFT) for similar angles fail to predict this feature.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the context of flat bands in TBG, presents the novel ARPES observation at the M point, compares this finding against predictions from both TB and DFT models, and concludes that the origin likely involves structural effects neglected by the current models.
why_interesting: The unexpected appearance of a correlated state (flat band) away from the magic angle and K point suggests that structural inhomogeneities or local distortions can induce novel correlated phases, expanding the parameter space for correlated electron physics.
